A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, during wound repair in epithelial sheets, cells in multiple rows are active in the repair process, and that the actomyosins that drive these processes are targeted to the same sites as in morphogenesis.
the wound edge advances by a process of cell intercalation, and that intercalation requires actomyosin-driven junction shrinkage in cells back from the leading edges.

The main takeaway from our work is that
wound re-epthelialisiation recapitulates morphogenetic cell rearrangement mechanisms and that these events are required for efficient wound repair.
the wound edge is not a static entity, but a dynamic structure that is actively driven by multiple cell rows back from the leading wound edge, which is a novel mechanism for tissue repair.

the actomyosins that assemble in the wound edge are not only responsible for the leading edge of the epithelial sheet, but also contribute to the contraction of the entire tissue to drive wound repair.
